newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In a report outlining its achievements after six months in office, the government is claiming credit for its handling of the current economic crisis while blaming previous administrations for the country's predicaments. The report, which the Chavalit government will use to announce its achievements to the nation on Thursday, is compiled by a working group chaired by Cabinet Secretary-General Visanu Kreua-ngam. (BANGKOK POST)

- Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh has hinted at support for the Chart Pattana Party in its expected face-off with Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan tomorrow over the party's request for a review of proposed excise taxes. The outcome of tomorrow's Cabinet meeting, which Chavalit confirmed will tackle the politically-sensitive issue, is crucial to the future of the government, whose much-criticised economic performance is lagely attributed to Amnuay-Chart Pattana rivalry. (THE NATION)

- Police has denied that a man who was shot dead early Saturday was a witness in the Taurus Pub shooting. The victim was shot dead by a gunman in the middle of a bridge and a black baseball bat was found near his body. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- Eastern Sugar Co and Singapore's JTC International Pte are together spending 18 billion baht to develop Thailand's largest industrial estate. The joint-venture agreement is scheduled for signing today at Government House. Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and Singaporean counterpart Goh Chok Tong, who is due to arrive in Bangkok today, are to witness the signing. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- In response to a Government mandate, the Customs Department will install a new computer system in an effort to increase efficiency of operations and reduce corruption. Streamlining customs operations and cutting red tape have been mandated by the Government. (BUSINESS DAY)
